newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: English premier league matches scheduled for Wednesday (kick-off times 1500 GMT unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Postponed due to weather: Derby (11) v Sheffield Wednesday (9), Leicester (12) v Tottenham Hotspur (10).
Arsenal (3) v Middlesbrough (17)

Arsenal need to revive their title bid. Saturday's 2-2 home draw with Aston Villa was their fourth consecutive match without a win. Striker Ian Wright plays his last game before beginning a three-match ban. A booking could increase it to five. Lee Dixon and David Platt are both still injured.

Middlesbrough, rocked by a 3-0 defeat at Coventry on Saturday and unsettled by Real Madrid's interest in Brazilian midfielder Juninho, have an injury crisis. Steve Vickers (calf), Phil Whelan (hamstring) and Phil Stamp are doubtful. Midfielder Robbie Mustoe returns from suspension, but Derek Whyte is out. Coach Bryan Robson, 40 next month, may have to pick himself.
Chelsea (7) v Liverpool (1)

Chelsea need to improve from their 2-2 home draw with Sheffield Wednesday. Coach Ruud Gullit is re-shaping his squad. Irish left-back Terry Phelan has just left for Everton and Chelsea have been linked to Tottenham's unsettled England striker Teddy Sheringham.
Liverpool, back to winning form at Southampton on Sunday, have in-form striker Robbie Fowler back from an ankle injury as they seek a seventh away win in 11 outings.
Coventry (14) v Sunderland (13)
Coventry are likely to be unchanged after four successive victories which have hauled them out of the relegation zone.

Sunderland's injury-hit squad was dealt another blow when striker Craig Russell limped off after 25 minutes of their defeat at West Ham on Saturday. Coach Peter Reid has lamented his players' attitude after seven defeats and only seven goals in 10 away games.
Everton (8) v Blackburn Rovers (18) 1745 GMT

Everton's Scottish international striker Duncan Ferguson injured a hamstring in the home defeat by Wimbledon and may be sidelined. Central defender David Unsworth is out. He starts a two-match ban on Wednesday. Terry Phelan, signed from Chelsea for 850,000 pounds, goes straight into the side to replace injured England left-back Andy Hinchcliffe. Russian winger Andrei Kanchelskis returns after missing Everton's last two games with influenza.
Blackburn, climbing slowly away from the foot of the table under caretaker-coach Tony Parkes, are likely to be unchanged as they bid for their first away win after two consecutive clean sheets.
Manchester United (2) v Aston Villa (6) 2000 GMT

The biggest crowd at a premier league match this season saw Manchester United beat Leeds last Saturday and rekindle their title challenge. In their last three games United have scored 10 without reply. Irish midfielder Roy Keane and striker Andy Cole are back but United will be without defenders Gary Pallister (back injury) and Phil Neville (glandular fever).

Aston Villa, with only four points from their last three games, are likely to field the same side that twice came from behind to earn a point at Arsenal on Saturday. Midfielder Mark Draper is suffering a groin injury which requires surgery but is nevertheless likely to play.
Newcastle United (5) v Leeds United (15)

Newcastle broke a run of seven games without a win with a 7-1 rout of Tottenham. Shaka Hislop is set to continue in goal instead of Czech Pavel Srnicek. John Beresford is carrying a calf muscle injury. Warren Barton has recovered from a bout of influenza. David Ginola, Steve Howey (both calf) and Faustino Aspirilla (hamstring) are all out.

Leeds are improving despite their 1-0 defeat at Manchester United. Coach George Graham was heartened by the players' resolve at Old Trafford. The squad have had to find an alternative training ground as their usual venue was closed because of a gas leak. Ghanian striker Tony Yeboah may be sidelined again (hamstring).
Southampton (19) v Wimbledon (4)

England forward Matt Le Tissier is recovering from injury and has come on as substitute in Southampton's last two games. But a frozen pitch has meant he has not been able to train. Coach Graeme Souness hopes to complete the signing of Oxford defender Matthew Elliott this week.
Forward Robbie Earle is fit again for Wimbledon after missing their win at Everton with influenza. He will be added to an otherwise unchanged squad.
West Ham (16) v Nottingham Forest (20)

West Ham's Romanian striker Florin Raducioiu, who scored a spectacular goal in West Ham's 2-0 win over Sunderland, is likely to make the starting 11 again as the Londoners look to stay clear of the relegation zone. Compatriot Ilie Dumitrescu looks set to leave for Mexico.

Forest need a run of championship-winning form if they are to avoid relegation. Caretaker player-coach Stuart Pearce has set a target of 46 points requiring Forest to win 11 of their remaining 18 fixtures -- a tall order for a team which has won only twice in 20 league games.
